title: Lazy Task Registration, Dependencies, and Ordering Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies lazy task registration, dependencies, and ordering?
options: Keep TaskProvider values lazy and express task relationships through Provider-backed data flow.
Call get on every registered task
questions.answer: Keep TaskProvider values lazy and express task relationships through Provider-backed data flow.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: mustRunAfter causes the referenced task to be added to the graph.
questions.explanation: Calling schema.get().outputFile during configuration realises the producer and discards the automatic lazy wiring available through flatMap.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to connect two file-producing tasks?
questions.answer: Set the consumer input from the producer output Provider so Gradle infers the task dependency.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
